### SEO-001: Browser `<title>` Tag Renders as "Social Media Platforms" Site-wide

- **Status:** ✅ Already Working
- **Priority:** Critical
- **Category:** Technical SEO / Metadata
- **Evidence:**
  - `analyze_page.py` result for `/`: `"title": "Social Media Platforms", "title_ok": false`
  - `analyze_page.py` result for `/blogs`: `"title": "Social Media Platforms", "title_ok": false`
  - `analyze_page.py` result for `/pricing`: `"title": "Social Media Platforms", "title_ok": false`
  - `app/social-media-platforms/page.tsx` exports `metadata.title = "Social Media Platforms | SpaceLean"` — this appears to be bleeding into the `<title>` tag across all pages via a rendering or caching anomaly.
  - `app/layout.tsx` line 18 defines the correct default title `"SpaceLean | AI-Powered Lean Project Management & Construction Scheduling Software"`, but it is not surfacing in rendered HTML.
- **Files Involved:**
  - `app/social-media-platforms/page.tsx`
  - `app/layout.tsx`
  - `app/page.tsx`
  - `app/blogs/page.tsx`
  - `app/pricing/page.tsx`
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. Run the site locally and inspect the `<head>` rendered HTML of `/`, `/blogs`, `/pricing` in the browser DevTools.
  2. Check whether `app/social-media-platforms/page.tsx` is using a global side-effect (e.g., `document.title` manipulation via `useEffect`) or if there is a shared layout that incorrectly inherits this page's metadata.
  3. Ensure all page-level `metadata` exports use the `title` field correctly and that no `useEffect` or client-side code overwrites `document.title` globally.
  4. Verify with `analyze_page.py` after fixing: `"title_ok": true`.
- **Expected SEO Impact:** 🔴 Catastrophic — Google indexes `"Social Media Platforms"` as the title for every page, completely destroying keyword targeting and SERP click-through rates for the entire site.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - `analyze_page.py https://spacelean.ai` returns `"title": "SpaceLean | AI-Powered Lean Project Management & Construction Scheduling Software"`.
  - Each page renders its own unique title in browser DevTools `<head>`.
  - No page title reads "Social Media Platforms" unless it is the social-media-platforms page itself.

### SEO-003: No Analytics / Conversion Tracking Detected

- **Status:** ❌ Missing
- **Priority:** Critical
- **Category:** Technical SEO / Performance Monitoring
- **Evidence:**
  - `analyze_page.py` scores `"tracking": 3/10` for all pages scanned.
  - `"tools_detected": []` — no Google Analytics 4, GTM, Plausible, Fathom, or Posthog found in rendered HTML.
  - Searched entire codebase (`app/`, `components/`) for `gtag`, `G-`, `UA-`, `googletagmanager`, `plausible`, `mixpanel` — zero results.
  - `app/privacy/page.tsx` mentions "anonymized analytics" but no implementation exists in code.
- **Files Involved:**
  - `app/layout.tsx` (where analytics should be added)
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. Implement Google Analytics 4 (GA4) via the Next.js `@next/third-parties` package (`GoogleAnalytics` component) or via a `<Script>` tag in `app/layout.tsx`.
  2. Alternatively, use privacy-first analytics (Plausible, Fathom) — add the tracking script to `app/layout.tsx`.
  3. Configure conversion goals: form submissions on `/request-a-demo`, CTA clicks on "Start Free Trial", and tool usage on `/tool`.
  4. Submit the property to Google Search Console (GSC) — the `verification.google` token already exists in `app/layout.tsx` line 90, so GSC property connection is likely set up, but data requires the tracking script.
- **Expected SEO Impact:** High (indirect) — Without analytics, there is no data to make informed SEO decisions, no Core Web Vitals field data, and no conversion attribution for SEO campaigns.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - `analyze_page.py` detects at least one analytics tool in `"tools_detected"`.
  - GA4 or equivalent sends pageview events on `/`, `/pricing`, `/blogs`.
  - Conversion events fire on CTA clicks.

### SEO-006: Fake/Unverified `aggregateRating` Schema Used Across Multiple Pages

- **Status:** ❌ Risks Google Penalty
- **Priority:** High
- **Category:** Structured Data / Schema Integrity
- **Evidence:**
  - `app/page.tsx` lines 64–70: `"ratingValue": "4.8", "reviewCount": "127"` — no visible review source on the page.
  - `app/pricing/page.tsx` lines 42–46: same `4.8/127` values — no reviews displayed.
  - `app/tool/page.tsx` lines 67–71: same `4.8/127` values.
  - `app/features/page.tsx` lines 105–108: same `4.8/127` values.
  - `app/compare/[slug]/page.tsx` lines 151–154: `"ratingValue": "4.9", "reviewCount": "340"` — different inflated values with no source.
  - Google's schema guidelines require that `aggregateRating` data **matches visible content on the page**. Fake ratings can result in manual actions.
  - `components/Testimonials.tsx` has 3 testimonials from fictional personas ("Sarah Jenkins, TechFlow"; "Michael Chen, StartupX"; "Emily Rodriguez, Marketing Lead") — not real verifiable reviews.
- **Files Involved:**
  - `app/page.tsx`, `app/pricing/page.tsx`, `app/tool/page.tsx`, `app/features/page.tsx`, `app/compare/[slug]/page.tsx`
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. **Remove all `aggregateRating` schema** from all pages immediately. This is the safest path to avoid a Google manual action for fake structured data.
  2. Alternatively, source real reviews from G2, Capterra, or Trustpilot, display the actual ratings and review counts visibly on the page, and then reflect the real figures in schema.
  3. Update `components/Testimonials.tsx` to use real customer names with verifiable companies, or remove the names if they are composites.
- **Expected SEO Impact:** Removing fake ratings prevents potential Google penalties. Implementing real ratings from verified review platforms earns rich snippets (stars in SERPs), which significantly increases CTR.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - All `aggregateRating` schema is either removed or backed by real, visible, verifiable review data.
  - No conflicting values (4.8 vs 4.9, 127 vs 340) across pages for the same product.
  - Google's Rich Results Test passes for all affected pages.

### SEO-007: OG Image Uses Relative Path (May Fail Social Sharing)

- **Status:** 🔶 Partial
- **Priority:** High
- **Category:** Open Graph / Social Metadata
- **Evidence:**
  - `app/layout.tsx` line 61: `url: "/marketing.jpg"` — relative path in OG image.
  - `metadataBase` is set correctly (line 88: `new URL("https://spacelean.ai")`), which means Next.js should resolve it, but some social crawlers (LinkedIn, Slack) fail to resolve relative OG image URLs when `metadataBase` is used.
  - Confirmed by `analyze_page.py`: `"og:image": "https://spacelean.ai/marketing.jpg"` — the script *does* see the absolute URL, but this relies on Next.js rendering at crawl time.
  - `app/layout.tsx` Twitter image line 73: `images: ["/marketing.jpg"]` — also relative.
- **Files Involved:**
  - `app/layout.tsx` lines 61, 73
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. Change OG image `url` to the fully qualified URL: `"https://spacelean.ai/marketing.jpg"`.
  2. Change Twitter `images` to: `["https://spacelean.ai/marketing.jpg"]`.
  3. Verify with the [Twitter Card Validator](https://cards-dev.twitter.com/validator) and [Facebook Sharing Debugger](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/) after deploying.
- **Expected SEO Impact:** Medium — Ensures correct social share preview images on LinkedIn, Slack, WhatsApp, and Twitter/X, improving organic referral traffic from content sharing.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - OG image URL is fully qualified (`https://spacelean.ai/marketing.jpg`).
  - Facebook Sharing Debugger and Twitter Card Validator render the correct preview image.

### SEO-009: `SoftwareApplication` Schema Defined Twice in Homepage (Duplicate Schema)

- **Status:** ❌ Issue
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Category:** Structured Data / Schema Integrity
- **Evidence:**
  - `app/layout.tsx` lines 120–136: Defines `SoftwareApplication` schema globally.
  - `app/page.tsx` lines 38–129: Defines another `SoftwareApplication` schema for the homepage specifically.
  - Both schemas are injected into the homepage's `<head>` as separate `<script type="application/ld+json">` blocks, creating duplicate entity declarations.
  - `analyze_page.py` confirms: `"schema_types": ["Organization", "SoftwareApplication", "SoftwareApplication", "Organization", "VideoObject", "VideoObject", "FAQPage"]` — two `SoftwareApplication` and two `Organization` blocks.
  - The homepage-level `SoftwareApplication` in `app/page.tsx` has richer content (featureList, offers, publisher) but conflicts with the layout-level one.
- **Files Involved:**
  - `app/layout.tsx` lines 120–136
  - `app/page.tsx` lines 38–129
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. Remove the `SoftwareApplication` schema from `app/layout.tsx` (keep only `Organization` and `WebSite` in layout).
  2. Keep the richer `SoftwareApplication` schema in `app/page.tsx` since it is homepage-specific and has more detailed data.
  3. Consolidate `Organization` schema: only keep in layout, remove from `app/page.tsx` lines 131–152 (or vice versa — pick one source of truth).
- **Expected SEO Impact:** Medium — Duplicate entity schemas can confuse Google's Knowledge Panel extraction and structured data processing. Clean separation ensures accurate rich result eligibility.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - Homepage has exactly one `SoftwareApplication` and one `Organization` JSON-LD block.
  - Google's Rich Results Test shows no duplicate entity warnings.

### SEO-010: `sitemap.ts` Uses `lastModified: new Date()` (Always Today)

- **Status:** 🔶 Partial
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Category:** Technical SEO / Crawl Budget
- **Evidence:**
  - `app/sitemap.ts` — every single URL (static, blog, solution, comparison, core feature) uses `lastModified: new Date()`, which always resolves to the current timestamp at render time.
  - This tells Google every page was modified today, every day — which is factually false for most pages and trains Googlebot to distrust the `lastModified` signal.
  - Blog posts have actual dates in `lib/blog-data.ts` (`post.date`, `post.updatedAt`) but are not used in the sitemap.
  - Noted in GEO-005 (in `GEO_OPTIMIZATION_TASKS.md`) for schema but not for the sitemap itself.
- **Files Involved:**
  - `app/sitemap.ts` lines 119–123, 128–133, 137–142, 146–151
  - `lib/blog-data.ts` (source of real dates)
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. For blog pages: use `new Date(post.updatedAt ?? post.date)` as `lastModified`.
  2. For solution pages: use a static date or the solution data's last-edited date.
  3. For static pages (homepage, pricing, etc.): use a real date that reflects the last meaningful content change, not `new Date()`.
  4. Keep `lastModified: new Date()` only for truly dynamic pages (e.g., `/rss.xml`).
- **Expected SEO Impact:** Medium — Accurate `lastModified` dates improve crawl prioritization, reduce wasted crawl budget, and help Google discover genuine content updates faster.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - Blog `lastModified` values use `post.updatedAt ?? post.date` (real dates, not today).
  - Static pages use pinned dates (or deploy-time dates via env var) rather than `new Date()`.
  - Sitemap XML contains date-varied entries, not identical timestamps for all URLs.

### SEO-016: Testimonials Use Fictional Company Names — E-E-A-T Risk

- **Status:** 🔶 Partial
- **Priority:** High
- **Category:** E-E-A-T / Trust Signals
- **Evidence:**
  - `components/Testimonials.tsx` lines 9–27: three testimonials with companies `"TechFlow"`, `"StartupX"`, and `"Marketing Lead"` (no company) — none are real, verifiable companies.
  - Google's E-E-A-T guidelines score "Trustworthiness" lower for sites with unverifiable social proof.
  - The testimonials reference generic productivity outcomes (40% productivity improvement) not construction-specific results.
  - Solution pages (`components/solutions/SolutionDetailClient.tsx` line 364) do support a `solution.testimonial` field — but it requires real data in `lib/solutions-data.ts`.
- **Files Involved:**
  - `components/Testimonials.tsx`
  - `lib/solutions-data.ts`
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. Replace fictional testimonials with real customer quotes. If no real customers have provided quotes yet, replace with: (a) beta tester feedback with first-name + role only, or (b) remove the testimonial carousel until real quotes are available.
  2. If using real testimonials, add:
     - Full name + company name + verified role
     - Company logo if permitted
     - Link to the company's LinkedIn or website for verifiability
  3. Add `Review` JSON-LD schema to the homepage if real testimonials are displayed.
- **Expected SEO Impact:** Medium (direct) / High (indirect) — Google may discount fake social proof signals. Real testimonials improve conversion rates, which improves behavioral signals (lower bounce rate, longer dwell time) that feed back into rankings.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - All testimonials reference real, verifiable people and companies (or are removed).
  - Company names, if displayed, are Googleable real entities.
  - No generic company names like "TechFlow" or "StartupX".

## Phase 5: Performance and Ongoing SEO Monitoring

### SEO-021: Core Web Vitals — No Field Data Due to Missing Analytics

- **Status:** ❌ Cannot Measure
- **Priority:** High
- **Category:** Performance / Core Web Vitals
- **Evidence:**
  - No analytics tracking detected (see SEO-003), so Google cannot collect real-user Core Web Vitals (CrUX) data.
  - Without CrUX data, the site has no "Good URL" classification in Google Search Console.
  - Lab data (Lighthouse scores) are available via `analyze_page.py` indirectly, but field data is required for Google's ranking algorithm.
  - Known performance risks from codebase: heavy 3D model files in `/public` (`city_pack_8.glb`: 3.5MB, `city_pack_8_original.glb`: 13.3MB), large video files (`175571-853887894_medium.mp4`: 1.4MB), and 14 JavaScript script tags on the homepage.
- **Files Involved:**
  - `app/layout.tsx` (analytics integration)
  - `public/city_pack_8.glb`, `public/city_pack_8_original.glb` (large binary assets)
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. Implement analytics first (SEO-003) to start collecting CrUX field data.
  2. Run PageSpeed Insights on all core pages: `/`, `/pricing`, `/blogs`, `/tool`.
  3. Address any LCP, INP, or CLS failures.
  4. Lazy-load the 3D model viewer — ensure `.glb` files are not preloaded.
  5. Use Next.js `<Image>` component for all images in components that currently use `<img>` (see SEO-022).
- **Expected SEO Impact:** High — Google's Core Web Vitals are a confirmed ranking signal. Pages passing all three CWV metrics see 24% fewer page abandonments and rank higher in competitive SERPs.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - All core pages score "Good" (green) for LCP, INP, and CLS in PageSpeed Insights field data.
  - CrUX data begins appearing in GSC within 28 days of analytics implementation.

### SEO-022: Some Components Use `<img>` Instead of Next.js `<Image>` (LCP Risk)

- **Status:** ❌ Missing
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Category:** Performance / Image Optimization
- **Evidence:**
  - `components/CareersClient.tsx` lines 168, 175, 184: uses `<img>` tag.
  - `components/Dashboardshowcase.tsx` line 112: uses `<img>` tag.
  - `components/ToolsSection.tsx` line 292: uses `<img>` tag.
  - `components/WhyUs.tsx` line 152: uses `<img>` tag.
  - `components/FeaturesClient.tsx` line 109: uses `<img>` tag.
  - `components/about/AboutTeam.tsx` lines 66, 105, 143: uses `<img>` tag.
  - Next.js `<Image>` provides automatic WebP conversion, lazy loading, responsive srcsets, and prevents CLS by requiring width/height.
- **Files Involved:**
  - `components/CareersClient.tsx`, `components/Dashboardshowcase.tsx`, `components/ToolsSection.tsx`, `components/WhyUs.tsx`, `components/FeaturesClient.tsx`, `components/about/AboutTeam.tsx`
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. Replace `<img>` tags with Next.js `<Image>` components in all non-SVG, non-inline images.
  2. Add explicit `width` and `height` props to prevent CLS.
  3. Use `priority` prop only for above-the-fold hero images (LCP element).
  4. Use `loading="lazy"` default for below-fold images.
- **Expected SEO Impact:** Medium — Improves LCP score by deferring off-screen images, reduces bandwidth, and prevents cumulative layout shifts that harm CLS.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - All content images in the 6 identified components use Next.js `<Image>`.
  - CLS score does not regress after changes.
  - PageSpeed Insights does not flag "Properly size images" for any of these components.

### SEO-023: No Google Search Console Submission Confirmed for Sitemap

- **Status:** Needs Verification
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Category:** Technical SEO / Indexing
- **Evidence:**
  - `public/robots.txt` correctly references the sitemap: `Sitemap: https://spacelean.ai/sitemap.xml`.
  - `app/robots.ts` also outputs the sitemap reference.
  - `analyze_page.py` confirms: `"sitemap": {"exists": true, "url_count": 83}`.
  - However, there is no code-level or documented evidence that the sitemap has been submitted to Google Search Console or Bing Webmaster Tools.
  - The `verification.google` token in `app/layout.tsx` line 90 (`"fZiGZZYWb8sosgKhEut7JJEHdH1KGKEAiEmgUYtGMqY"`) suggests GSC is set up, but sitemap submission requires a manual action in the GSC dashboard.
- **Files Involved:**
  - External action (Google Search Console dashboard)
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. Log into Google Search Console and submit `https://spacelean.ai/sitemap.xml`.
  2. Submit to Bing Webmaster Tools as well.
  3. Monitor "Coverage" report in GSC for any indexing errors (404s, soft 404s, redirect chains).
  4. Request indexing for the top priority pages: `/`, `/pricing`, `/tool`, `/compare/*`, `/solutions/*`.
- **Expected SEO Impact:** Medium — Ensures all 83 URLs in the sitemap are discovered and queued for indexing. Speeds up indexing of new content.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - GSC shows sitemap submitted with 83 URLs discovered.
  - No more than 5% of submitted URLs show as "Excluded" or "Error".

### SEO-024: No Structured SEO Monitoring Cadence Defined

- **Status:** ❌ Missing
- **Priority:** Low
- **Category:** Ongoing SEO Operations
- **Evidence:**
  - No monitoring scripts, cron jobs, or GSC integration exist in the codebase.
  - The skill recommends a publishing cadence and content update strategy.
  - `analyze_page.py` can be run on a schedule to track SEO scores over time.
- **Recommended Implementation:**
  1. Schedule `analyze_page.py` to run weekly against key pages and log scores to a CSV.
  2. Set up GSC weekly email reports for search performance, coverage, and Core Web Vitals.
  3. Define a monthly blog publishing goal (minimum 2 construction-focused posts per month).
  4. Set up automated broken link checks using a tool like `linkchecker` or a GSC coverage alert.
  5. Create a quarterly content refresh checklist: update `dateModified` in schema, refresh statistics and examples, update competitor comparison data.
- **Expected SEO Impact:** Low (immediate) / High (cumulative) — Consistent monitoring prevents regressions and ensures SEO gains compound over time.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - Weekly `analyze_page.py` runs are scheduled with output logged.
  - Monthly blog publishing target is documented and tracked.
  - GSC performance reports are reviewed at least monthly.
